It has been realized that the PLK condition is satisfied in rather  broad settings. In particular, it holds at every 
nonstationary point of $f$, for semianalytic and more general functions known as definable in o-minimal structures; see, e.g., \cite{AbsilMahonyAndrews2005,AttouchBolteRedontSoubeyran2010,AttouchBolteSvaiter2013} and the references therein. \end{Remark}

declaration_text: If the gradient of a differentiable function is L-Lipschitz on the segment joining x and y, then |f(y)-f(x)-<∇f(x),y-x>| ≤ (L/2)||y-x||². This is the cited descent lemma recalled in B0011.

nodes.title: 标准PLK下降收敛准则
declaration_text: For a C¹ function and an iterate sequence, eventual primary descent f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1}) ≥ σ||∇f(x^k)|| ||x^{k+1}-x^k|| together with complementary descent f(x^{k+1})=f(x^k) ⇒ x^{k+1}=x^k ensures convergence to an accumulation point at which the PLK property holds. This is the cited criterion recalled in B0019.

nodes.title: 标准指数PLK速率定理
declaration_text: Under eventual sufficient quadratic descent and the gradient-step bound stated in B0022, an accumulation point satisfying PLK with desingularizing function Mt^(1-q) gives finite termination for 0<q<1/2, linear iterate convergence for q=1/2, and iterate error O(k^(-(1-q)/(2q-1))) for 1/2<q<1. The local smooth-domain application for an already convergent sequence is as recalled in B0024.

nodes.title: 标准收敛速率转换
declaration_text: For a convergent sequence in an open convex domain where ∇f is Lipschitz, if a||∇f(x^k)||² ≤ f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1}) eventually for a>0, linear iterate convergence gives linear function-value and gradient convergence; iterate error O(m(k)) with m(k) decreasing to zero gives function-value error O(m(k)²) and gradient norm O(m(k)). This is the cited result recalled in B0045.

nodes.title: 初等分析与欧氏空间事实
declaration_text: Use the triangle, Cauchy–Schwarz, AM–GM and elementary squared-norm inequalities; convergence of geometric series with ratio in [0,1); convergence of Euclidean sequences with summable successive distances; continuity and differentiation of smooth functions; zero gradient at an interior differentiable local minimizer; reduction of smooth subdifferentials to the gradient; and elementary integration, monotonicity and first-order inequalities for differentiable concave functions.
